summary: A 1977 Telnet option for the SUPDUP protocol, letting a Telnet connection switch to SUPDUP mode. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This lets a plain chat connection upgrade to a fancier display protocol if both sides agree.

questions: what is the telnet supdup option
what is the telnet option code for supdup
subtitle: A Telnet option code that lets two hosts agree to switch a connection over to the SUPDUP display protocol.

tldr.problem: A Telnet connection had no standard way to announce that both sides want to use the SUPDUP display protocol.
tldr.mechanism: The SUPDUP option (code 21) uses the usual WILL, WON'T, DO and DON'T commands to ask for, grant or refuse use of the SUPDUP protocol.
tldr.outcome: The default is that SUPDUP is not in use, so it only applies once the two sides agree.

today: RFC 736 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata records no RFC obsoleting or updating it. RFC 749 builds on it with an option that carries SUPDUP display output inside Telnet.

sections.title: The SUPDUP Option
sections.content: RFC 736, by Mark Crispin, defines a TELNET option named SUPDUP with code 21. The option is a negotiation hook for the SUPDUP display protocol. The text is only a short option definition: a name and code, the meaning of the commands, and a default.
sections.plainLanguage: This gives the fancy screen language a name tag, number 21, so computers can ask for it.

sections.title: Command Meanings
sections.content:
IAC WILL SUPDUP requests permission to, or confirms it will, use the SUPDUP display protocol. IAC WON'T SUPDUP refuses to use it. IAC DO SUPDUP requests that the receiver use it, or grants the receiver permission to use it.

The fourth command, a demand that the receiver not use the protocol, is printed in the RFC as IAC DON'T with the option name missing, which is an evident omission in the text.
sections.plainLanguage: One side asks 'can I use it?', the other says yes or no, and either can ask the other to start.

sections.title: Default
sections.content: The default is WON'T SUPDUP and DON'T SUPDUP, meaning the SUPDUP display protocol is not in use. Until both sides agree through these commands, the connection stays an ordinary Telnet connection.
sections.plainLanguage: Unless both say yes, nothing changes and you keep talking the plain way.
